title: Elimination of normalized linear polynomial variables
statement: Let $K$ be a commutative ring, $\sigma$ a type with decidable equality, $E\subseteq\sigma$ a finite subset, $a\in K^\times$, and $h:\sigma\times\sigma\to K$. Assume $h(l,j)=a\delta_{lj}$ for $l,j\in E$. In the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] let $I=(aX_l-\sum_{j\in E}h(l,j)X_j:l\in\sigma)$. Then there exists a $K$-algebra isomorphism $K[X_j:j\in E]\cong K[X_l:l\in\sigma]/I$, with quotient understood as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 07CP (lemma-lifting), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07CP; read from the online tag because the local TeX is absent.

proof.text: Let q be the quotient map and define F on the free polynomial ring by F(X_j)=q(X_j). Define v_l=X_l for l in E and v_l=a inverse times sum over j in E of h(l,j)X_j otherwise. Evaluation at v defines G0 on the full polynomial ring.
For l in E normalization reduces the sum to a X_l; for l outside E multiply a by its inverse. Thus G0 kills every generator of I and hence I. It factors to G on the quotient.

G F fixes all free variables and coefficients. For F G, the relation q(a X_l)=sum h(l,j) q(X_j) and invertibility of a show every complementary variable is fixed; free variables are fixed by construction. Polynomial extensionality and quotient surjectivity prove the two composites are identities.

proof_origin.note: Details of the displayed calculation in Stacks Tag 07CP, written by N1.

lean.statement: theorem linear_elimination (K : Type u) [CommRing K] (σ : Type v) [DecidableEq σ] (E : Finset σ) (a : Kˣ) (h : σ → σ → K) (hnorm : ∀ l : E, ∀ j : E, h l j = if l = j then (a : K) else 0) : Nonempty (MvPolynomial E K ≃ₐ[K] (MvPolynomial σ K ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun l : σ ↦ C (a : K) * X l - ∑ j : E, C (h l j) * X (j : σ)))))
